content.introduction: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is a unit of the United States Department of Labor, formed on June 27, 1884. It is the principal fact-finding agency for the U.S. government in the broad field of labor economics and statistics and serves as a principal agency of the U.S. federal statistical system. The BLS collects, processes, analyzes, and disseminates essential statistical data to the American public, the U.S. Congress, other Federal agencies, state and local governments, businesses, and labor representatives. The headquarters of the BLS is located at the Suitland Federal Center in Suitland, Maryland, U.S. The agency has 2,100 employees and an annual budget of $697.9 million (FY2025 enacted). The current Commissioner is Brett Matsumoto, and the Deputy Commissioner is William J. Wiatrowski.
